analysis_md:
# DTE — DTE Energy Company
v5 run, 2026-10-14. In scope (market cap $26,560.2M at $128.31, nasdaq_quote_api, per dcf_numbers.json).

All figures below are copied from dcf_numbers.json, ttm.py output (ttm.json), financials_history.csv, or the company's FY2025 10-K as cited — none are recomputed. Guidance and quarter figures are from cited search results, as noted.

## What it is
Detroit-based regulated utility holding company. DTE Electric is an electric utility serving approximately 2.3 million customers in southeastern Michigan (generation, purchase, distribution and sale of electricity; regulated by the MPSC, FERC, NRC and EPA — FY2025 10-K, Electric segment description). DTE Gas is the regulated gas utility; DTE Vantage runs non-utility businesses (renewable natural gas and custom energy solutions); Energy Trading is the power marketing arm (segment operating results in the FY2025 10-K and Q2 2026 reporting, search results). Essentially all earnings are regulated or contract-backed. Management's plan is rate-base compounding: a $36.5B capital investment plan for 2026-2030, 2026 operating EPS guidance of $7.59 to $7.73 (reaffirmed after Q2 2026, with management saying in September 2026 it is positioned for the high end), and a long-term operating EPS growth target of 6% to 8% through 2030 (search results).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv and dcf_numbers.json):** net income $1,462M; operating cash flow $3,409M; capex $4,639M (tag: OVERRIDE — filing-sourced, see the DATA_GAP resolution below); SBC $60M (tag: OVERRIDE — filing-sourced, Note 21); D&A $1,841M; diluted shares 207,000,000. financials_history.csv carries no revenue after FY2017 (the filer discontinued the SalesRevenueNet tag the engine reads), so no revenue figure is quoted here rather than calculated.
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: −$1,290M = −$6.23/share** (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_total_latest_fy −$1,290,000,000; base_oe_latest_per_share −$6.2319). Capex exceeds operating cash flow — structural for a utility in a heavy rate-base build, not a one-off year: 2026 is guided to roughly $3.9B of operating cash flow against $6.8B of capital expenditures (search results), so the gap widens before it narrows.
- **OE positive 0 of the last 5 fiscal years** (dcf_numbers.json; oe_conservative from financials_history.csv, with the filing overrides applied): FY2021 −$1,632M / FY2022 −$2,722M / FY2023 −$1,479M / FY2024 −$1,056M / FY2025 −$1,290M.
- Maintenance version FY2025: $1,208M (financials_history.csv, oe_maintenance) — positive, and that gap between the two definitions is the story: most utility capex is growth capex that enters rate base and earns an authorized return, so the conservative definition (OCF − total capex − SBC) is the harsher yardstick, and it is the sweep's base case.
- **Base used in the final run = the TTM base from ttm.json: −$6.75/share** (base_source ttm_json; see STALE_FY below). The engine's normalized base (median of last 3 FY OE/share) is −$6.23/share (dcf_numbers.json: base_oe_normalized_per_share −$6.2319) and the latest FY alone is also −$6.23/share — every defensible base is negative, so the choice among them does not change the verdict.
- Balance sheet: net debt $25,098M (dcf_numbers.json: net_debt_latest $25,098,000,000). Share count is growing at a 1.84% CAGR (dcf_numbers.json: share_cagr 0.0184) — recurring equity issuance funds part of the capital plan and dilutes per-share compounding; the company plans a further $500-600M of equity issuance per year through 2028 (search results).

## Moat: 6/10 — durable regulated monopoly, capped economics
Justification: Franchised regulated monopolies — DTE Electric (approximately 2.3 million customers in southeastern Michigan, per the FY2025 10-K) and DTE Gas — with captive, essential-service demand, plus DTE Vantage (renewable natural gas / custom energy solutions) and Energy Trading. The rate-base model converts the $36.5B 2026-2030 capital plan into regulated earnings (management guides 6-8% operating EPS growth through 2030, search results), and large-load data-center agreements (1.4 GW Oracle approved and under construction; 1.0 GW Google executed, pending MPSC approval) add visible load growth. Capped at 6 because the MPSC sets the allowed return and has disallowed previously recorded capex (write-offs recorded in the FY2025 10-K), there is no pricing power beyond rate cases, and the plan is funded with debt (net debt $25,098M, dcf_numbers.json) plus planned equity issuance of $500-600M per year through 2028 (search results) that dilutes per-share compounding (share-count CAGR +1.84%/yr, dcf_numbers.json).
- FOR: Franchised regulated electric and gas monopolies in Michigan — DTE Electric serves ~2.3M customers in southeastern Michigan; captive, essential-service demand; the rate-base model turns the $36.5B 2026-2030 capital plan into authorized-return earnings, with 6-8% operating EPS growth guided through 2030; large-load growth is contracted (1.4 GW Oracle approved/under construction, 1.0 GW Google executed pending MPSC approval); recovery mechanisms (including the Infrastructure Recovery Mechanism for distribution spend) shorten the lag between capex and rate recovery.
- AGAINST: The MPSC sets allowed ROE and recovery and has disallowed capex before — the FY2025 10-K records write-offs of previously recorded capital expenditures from the December 2023 rate order (in 2023) and the January 2025 rate order (in 2024); affordability politics as data-center and clean-energy costs are recovered from existing customers; net debt $25,098M plus $500-600M/yr of planned equity issuance through 2028 dilutes the rate-base growth per share; coal retirement (all coal by 2032 per the 2026 Integrated Resource Plan, search results) and clean-energy mandates force transition capex whose full recovery is not guaranteed.
- A 6 gives CAP = 9.8 years by the sweep formula — academic here, since there is no positive OE stream to fade.

## DCF — v5 final run (2026-10-14)
The final engine pass was run with moat 6, default probabilities 10/25/30/25/10 (offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp, multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25) and the `--ttm` base pin, but **the engine emits no scenario table, IV, or IRR: the TTM base OE is −$6.75/share (normalized base −$6.23/share), so there is no positive owner's-earnings path to discount at any scenario weighting.** Tier by numbers: **F**.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | n/a | 0.75 | Adverse rate cases; MPSC disallowances grow; data-center approvals stall | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bear | 25% | n/a | 0.90 | Capex steps up to the guided $6.8B for 2026 while OCF lags; equity issuance accelerates | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Base | 30% | n/a | 1.00 | Capex > OCF indefinitely on the $36.5B plan; OE stays negative | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Bull | 25% | n/a | 1.10 | Rate-base growth and data-center load convert to distributable cash sooner than history suggests | n/a — negative base | n/a |
| Super bull | 10% | n/a | 1.25 | Structural FCF inflection | n/a — negative base | n/a |

- **Probability-weighted IV/IRR: not computable (negative base). Tier by numbers: F.**
- Sanity check on growth inputs: the engine's blended growth is 18.61% (dcf_numbers.json components: rev CAGR 5y 18.61%, rev CAGR 3y 18.61%, latest rev YoY 18.60%, OE/share CAGR 2y n/a). That blend is an artifact, not a current growth rate — the revenue series in financials_history.csv ends at FY2017 because the filer discontinued the SalesRevenueNet tag, so the revenue components are computed off a stale series. Management's actual guided growth is 6-8% operating EPS through 2030 (search results). Either way growth is irrelevant to the verdict: it multiplies a negative base. No scenario start was set below a recent print to manufacture conservatism, and none could rescue a negative base anyway.
- Recent prints (search results, for the record): Q2 2026 net income $282M, diluted EPS $1.35 (vs $229M / $1.10 in Q2 2025); operating EPS $1.32 vs $1.36 in Q2 2025; first-half 2026 net income $529M with operating earnings of $681M; 2026 operating EPS guidance reaffirmed at $7.59-$7.73. The earnings engine is healthy — it is the capex load, not profitability, that zeroes out conservative OE.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DATA_GAP:sbc and DATA_GAP:capex (initial run, exit 4)** — resolved with bounded filing overrides, not scored on gapped data. The override flags out-of-band mechanically (no filed value exists to band against) and carries an ack_reason saying exactly that. - **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025): structural, not a one-off. This is a capital-intensive regulated utility: OCF runs far above net income chiefly because depreciation is a large non-cash charge (D&A $1,606M in FY2023, $1,732M in FY2024 and $1,841M in FY2025, from financials_history.csv) added back in OCF, alongside deferred-tax and regulatory working-capital effects. No tax-deposit, impairment, or single-item swing explains or needs to explain the gap — it is the normal utility NI/OCF relationship. It does not distort the OE base either way: the conservative OE series is built from OCF directly, and it is capex, not the NI/OCF gap, that drives OE negative.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Utilities): accepted in full — the OE/capex DCF fits regulated utilities poorly, because growth capex is rate-base investment earning a regulated return, not value destruction. Confidence is graded **low** and the tier is read as "not modelable on this screen," not as "bad business."
- **OVERRIDE_APPLIED:sbc / OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex**: the two filing overrides above; each is registered with its measured impact by make_score.py, and neither replaces a filed value (none exists under the tags the engine reads).

## My thoughts / overlay
- This is the model's known blind spot, flagged as such — the same shape as AEE in this sweep: a profitable, dividend-paying regulated monopoly whose conservative owner's earnings are negative in all of the last 5 years, and on TTM, because utility capex runs above operating cash flow every year of a multi-year rate-base build (here supercharged by a $36.5B five-year plan and guided 2026 capex of $6.8B against $3.9B of guided operating cash flow, search results). The dividend and the build are funded the utility way — rate recovery plus continuous debt and equity issuance — which an OE screen reads as negative distributable cash.
- On numbers a utility investor actually uses (from search results, not the engine): 2026 operating EPS guided $7.59-$7.73 at a $128.31 price, long-term operating EPS growth guided 6-8% through 2030, and a declared quarterly dividend of $1.165 per share (annualized $4.66). That is a bond-like high-single-digit total-return profile before any multiple change — nowhere near Andrew's 15% hurdle on any defensible reading, so the F here agrees with the hurdle conclusion even though the model's mechanism (negative OE) is a sector artifact. No method range spanning tiers is claimed: on the v5 method, with the filing's own capex and SBC figures applied, there is one result, F. (The only "range" is the discredited one: zero-filling the missing capex/SBC manufactures a 25.17% weighted IRR on the measured counterfactual — that is the v4 failure mode the data gate exists to prevent, not a defensible input set.)
- Hurdle-clearing price: not computable from this model — with no positive OE base there is no IV@15% at any price, and stating one would require a different model (dividend / rate-base), which is out of scope for this sweep. No tier override: the numbers tier F is retained, with the mismatch documented, rather than inventing a tier the v5 method cannot support.
- Real risks for a holder (outside the model): MPSC disallowances and affordability pushback as data-center and clean-energy costs are recovered, approval risk on the 1.0 GW Google agreement, coal-retirement execution (all coal by 2032), and refinancing a $25,098M net-debt stack at current rates while issuing $500-600M/yr of new equity.
